vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: aicreditshare-platform
Version: 1.0.6

The skill bundle is a legitimate integration for the AI Credit Share platform, providing tools for task management, skill hiring, and account registration. The included shell scripts (aics.sh and init.sh) follow security best practices by using jq for safe JSON construction to prevent injection and implement standard HMAC-SHA256 authentication for API calls to aicreditshare.com. No evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized persistence, or malicious prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill largely does what its description says (automating actions against aicreditshare.com), but there are several inconsistencies and security concerns (undeclared dependencies, plaintext credential storage, and config-file writes) that you should be aware of before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description match the code and SKILL.md: it automates register/login/tasks/skills on https://www.aicreditshare.com. However registry metadata claimed no required binaries or config paths, while the shipped scripts actually require curl, jq and call openssl and read/write ~/.aicreditshare/config.json. Those undeclared requirements are a mismatch.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and examples call the platform APIs only (consistent). But the packaged scripts read and write a local config file (~/.aicreditshare/config.json) and persist API keys/secrets there; SKILL.md/registry did not declare that persistent local storage. SKILL.md lists allowed-tools: HTTP, but the skill relies on shell binaries (curl/jq/openssl) and local file I/O — a scope mismatch.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or remote downloads are present; the skill is instruction-only with two local scripts. This is the lowest-risk install mechanism (no arbitrary remote code fetched during install).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request external credentials via requires.env, which is appropriate. But it persistently stores agentApiKey/agentApiSecret in plaintext under ~/.aicreditshare/config.json (created by init.sh), exposing secrets on disk. There is an optional environment variable AICREDITSHARE_DEFAULT_PASSWORD referenced by init.sh but not declared in the metadata. Using plaintext storage and an undeclared env var are disproportionate to the claimed purpose without additional safeguards.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill creates and reads ~/.aicreditshare/config.json to save API keys/secrets. Although 'always' is false (no forced inclusion), the skill persists credentials on the user's home directory without setting file permissions or encryption. This persistent storage of secrets increases risk if other local users/processes can access the file.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to implement the advertised platform automation, but there are practical and security issues you should weigh: 1) The scripts expect curl, jq and openssl though the metadata doesn't declare them — ensure these are present and trustworthy. 2) init.sh writes API keys and secrets to ~/.aicreditshare/config.json in plaintext; if you install this, do not put sensitive or reused credentials there and inspect the file permissions (chmod 600). 3) The SKILL.md marks allowed-tools as HTTP, but the skill runs shell commands — consider whether you trust exported scripts that can run commands on your machine. 4) If you proceed, audit the scripts yourself (they are short and readable) and consider running them in a restricted environment (separate user account or sandbox) and using an account/secrets with limited funds/permissions. If any of these mismatches are unacceptable, do not install.
